description: Complete Gameplay Loop (ResourcePanel improvements, EventPanel improvements, Mission Outcome Overlays, Day Summary, Astro-AI hint upgrade) + Location Selection wired to simulation + Mission Duration wired to scoring. These three concerns are batched together because they all touch useMissionControl.ts and the simulation layer simultaneously, and must be done atomically to avoid two FEATs both editing the same hook.
steps: Step 1 — SIMULATION TYPES: Open src/simulation/types/index.ts. Add optional field to SimulationEngineConfig: readonly missionDurationDays?: number // default 90. This is the only change permitted in types/index.ts.

Step 2 — SIMULATION ENGINE: Open src/simulation/core/simulation-engine.ts. In the constructor, after the existing private field declarations, add: private readonly missionDurationDays: number. In the constructor body, after 'this.criticalFailureCount = 0', add: this.missionDurationDays = config.missionDurationDays ?? 90. In getMissionScore(), pass missionDurationDays to calculateMissionScore: update the scoringInput to include targetDurationDays: this.missionDurationDays. Update the ScoringInput import to include targetDurationDays.

Step 3 — MISSION SCORING: Open src/simulation/core/mission-scoring.ts. Add targetDurationDays?: number to ScoringInput interface (optional, default 90). In calculateMissionScore, after criticalFailurePenalty calculation, add: const targetDays = input.targetDurationDays ?? 90; const completionRatio = Math.min(daysRun / targetDays, 1.0); const durationBonus = Math.round(completionRatio * 100). Add durationBonus to finalScore computation. Add durationBonus field to MissionScore return type — also update the MissionScore interface in src/simulation/types/index.ts to include: readonly durationBonus: number.

Step 4 — LOCATION MODIFIER (NEW FILE): Create src/simulation/planets/location-modifier.ts. Export interface LocationModifier: { readonly id: string; readonly displayName: string; readonly planetId: 'moon' | 'mars'; readonly description: string; readonly solarIrradiance_factor: number; readonly radiationDelta_mSv: number; readonly temperatureMin_delta: number; readonly temperatureMax_delta: number; readonly dustFactor: number; readonly classificationNote: string }. Export function applyLocationModifier(profile: PlanetProfile, modifier: LocationModifier): PlanetProfile — returns a new PlanetProfile object with modified values: solarIrradiance_W_m2 *= modifier.solarIrradiance_factor, unshieldedDailyRadiation_mSv += modifier.radiationDelta_mSv, temperatureRange adjusted by deltas. Never mutates the input. Add source comment: '// EDUCATIONAL_ASSUMPTION — site-specific modifiers are approximations for educational gameplay'. Import PlanetProfile from '@simulation/types'.

Step 5 — MOON LOCATIONS (NEW FILE): Create src/data/locations/moon-locations.ts. Export MOON_LOCATIONS: readonly LocationModifier[] with 3 entries: { id: 'moon-equatorial', displayName: 'Equatorial Plains', planetId: 'moon', description: 'The classic lunar landing zone — extreme temperature swings but maximum solar power.', solarIrradiance_factor: 1.0, radiationDelta_mSv: 0, temperatureMin_delta: 0, temperatureMax_delta: 0, dustFactor: 1.0, classificationNote: 'EDUCATIONAL_ASSUMPTION — baseline equatorial site' }, { id: 'moon-polar', displayName: 'Polar Region', planetId: 'moon', description: 'Near the lunar poles — possible water ice but less solar power.', solarIrradiance_factor: 0.85, radiationDelta_mSv: 0, temperatureMin_delta: 20, temperatureMax_delta: -40, dustFactor: 0.9, classificationNote: 'EDUCATIONAL_ASSUMPTION — lunar polar lighting deficit from NASA LRO data' }, { id: 'moon-mare-imbrium', displayName: 'Mare Imbrium', planetId: 'moon', description: 'A vast ancient lava plain — good solar access but dustier than average.', solarIrradiance_factor: 0.95, radiationDelta_mSv: 0, temperatureMin_delta: 0, temperatureMax_delta: 0, dustFactor: 1.1, classificationNote: 'EDUCATIONAL_ASSUMPTION — mare regolith dust factor' }. Export getLocationById(id: string): LocationModifier | undefined.

Step 6 — MARS LOCATIONS (NEW FILE): Create src/data/locations/mars-locations.ts. Export MARS_LOCATIONS: readonly LocationModifier[] with 3 entries: { id: 'mars-gale-crater', displayName: 'Gale Crater', planetId: 'mars', description: 'Home of Curiosity rover — well-studied, stable baseline.', solarIrradiance_factor: 1.0, radiationDelta_mSv: 0, temperatureMin_delta: 0, temperatureMax_delta: 0, dustFactor: 1.0, classificationNote: 'EDUCATIONAL_ASSUMPTION — baseline from Curiosity mission data' }, { id: 'mars-jezero-crater', displayName: 'Jezero Crater', planetId: 'mars', description: 'Perseverance rover site — ancient river delta, slightly more dust.', solarIrradiance_factor: 0.92, radiationDelta_mSv: 0, temperatureMin_delta: 0, temperatureMax_delta: 0, dustFactor: 1.15, classificationNote: 'EDUCATIONAL_ASSUMPTION — based on Perseverance dust accumulation observations' }, { id: 'mars-olympus-mons', displayName: 'Olympus Mons Plateau', planetId: 'mars', description: 'The highest point on Mars — thinner atmosphere means less dust but higher radiation.', solarIrradiance_factor: 0.88, radiationDelta_mSv: 0.12, temperatureMin_delta: -10, temperatureMax_delta: -5, dustFactor: 0.5, classificationNote: 'EDUCATIONAL_ASSUMPTION — altitude effects on radiation and dust density' }. Export getLocationById(id: string): LocationModifier | undefined.

Step 7 — MISSION STORE: Add selectedLocationId: string | null (initial null) and selectedMissionDurationDays: number (initial 30) to MissionState in src/store/mission-store.ts. Add setSelectedLocation(locationId: string): void and setMissionDuration(days: 30 | 60 | 90): void actions. Update INITIAL_MISSION_STATE accordingly.

Step 8 — useMissionControl HOOK: In src/hooks/useMissionControl.ts: (a) Import getLocationById from '@data/locations/moon-locations' and '@data/locations/mars-locations'. Import applyLocationModifier from '@simulation/planets/location-modifier'. Import MOON_PROFILE from '@data/nasa/moon-profile' and MARS_PROFILE from '@data/nasa/mars-profile'. (b) Read selectedLocationId and selectedMissionDurationDays from missionStore in initializeMission(). (c) After validation checks, resolve the base planet profile, then look up selectedLocationId in the correct locations array (moon → MOON_LOCATIONS, mars → MARS_LOCATIONS). If found, apply applyLocationModifier(baseProfile, location) to get modifiedProfile, else use baseProfile unchanged. (d) Pass modifiedProfile as a new SimulationEngineConfig field — but wait: SimulationEngine currently reads planet from config.planetId and looks up profile internally. INSTEAD: Override the profile in the engine by passing missionDurationDays to the config. Do NOT change SimulationEngine to accept a custom profile (that would require touching simulation-engine.ts more than permitted). For the location effect, the solar factor from the location will be baked in differently. See constraint note below. (e) Pass missionDurationDays: selectedMissionDurationDays to SimulationEngineConfig. (f) Add selectedLocationId, selectedMissionDurationDays to the hook's return type and return values. CONSTRAINT NOTE: Since SimulationEngine reads planet profiles internally, the location modifier's solarIrradiance_factor cannot be injected directly. The correct additive approach: store the modifier's dustFactor as a multiplier the EventEngine sees via a new solarFactorModifier event consequence seeded at mission start. SIMPLER APPROACH (approved): On initializeMission(), if a non-baseline location is selected, immediately push a synthetic 'passive' event consequence into the engine's eventConsequences Map via a public method. Add a single public method to SimulationEngine: setBaselineSolarFactor(factor: number): void — this sets an initial effectiveSolarFactor override that persists until changed. This is the ONLY additional change to simulation-engine.ts beyond step 2.

Step 9 — RESOURCEPANEL IMPROVEMENTS: Update src/features/mission-control/ResourcePanel.tsx. For each resource bar: (a) Add transition-all duration-500 to the inner fill div of ResourceBar (check src/components/charts/ResourceBar.tsx and add this class to the fill element if not present). (b) Below each ResourceBar, add a small delta line showing daily change: compute delta from last 2 resourceHistory points. Show '+N.NN kg/day' or '-N.NN kg/day' in green/red. (c) Color the bar: green (#10B981) when > 50% of initial, amber (#F5A623) when 20-50%, red (#EF4444) when < 20%. Update ResourceBar component or pass status to it. (d) Add a critical warning banner at the top of the panel when ANY resource is < 15% of initial: a red Card accent='coral' strip reading '⚠️ Critical: {resourceName} running low!'.

Step 10 — EVENTPANEL IMPROVEMENTS: Update src/features/mission-control/EventPanel.tsx. The EventCard component in src/components/feedback/EventCard.tsx already exists — check its current implementation. (a) Add urgency visual: high-probability events (probability > 0.05) get red border (border-[#EF4444]), others yellow (border-[#F5A623]). Pass urgency to EventCard. (b) Verify the EventCard shows the affected resource icon, description, and TWO choice buttons. If EventCard doesn't have choice buttons, add them: map event.choices to buttons with variant='primary' for optimal choice and variant='secondary' for suboptimal. Each button calls onResolve(choice.id). (c) After resolving, show a result toast: create a simple toast state in EventPanel (useState<string | null>). After resolveEvent() call, set toast to the first explanation reason from the last SimulationResult. Display the toast as a small teal banner below the event card. Auto-dismiss after 4 seconds using useEffect with clearTimeout cleanup.

Step 11 — DAY SUMMARY: In MissionControlScreen.tsx, add a daySummary state: useState<SimulationResult | null>(null). In advanceDay (called from the hook), capture the result. Since useMissionControl hook doesn't return the raw SimulationResult, add lastSimResult: SimulationResult | null to the hook's return type and update the hook to store it in a useRef that is exposed. ALTERNATIVE: Add a onSimResult callback to the hook. SIMPLEST APPROACH: In MissionControlScreen, keep a local resultHistory ref and add an onDayAdvanced prop-less approach: after advanceDay() is called, check if currentMissionDay changed (via useEffect) and display the latest resourceHistory entry as the day summary. Show an inline card below the journey map for 3 seconds: 'Day N Summary: Oxygen -N kg, Water -N kg, Food -N kg, Energy -N kWh, events triggered'. Use useEffect watching currentMissionDay to trigger show/hide.

Step 12 — MISSION COMPLETION OVERLAY (success/partial): In MissionControlScreen.tsx, when missionOutcome changes to 'success' or 'partial', show a full-width teal overlay div with: 'Mission Complete!' heading, animated star rating (stars appear one by one via CSS animation — respect reducedMotion), '+N XP · Level up!' text computed from getXPForMission(stars, missionNumber), 'View Mission Report' button (→ /debrief), 'Continue' button that dismisses overlay. Add local showOutcomeOverlay state initialized to true when outcome !== 'ongoing'. The stars animation: use setTimeout to add stars one by one with 300ms delay each; skip animation when reducedMotion is true.

Step 13 — MISSION FAILURE OVERLAY: In MissionControlScreen.tsx, when missionOutcome changes to 'failure', show a dark overlay with: 'Mission Failed' heading, list of which fault states caused failure (from activeFaultStates), 'Try Again' button that calls resetMission() + navigate('/select-planet'), 'View Report' button that calls handleEndMission() + navigate('/debrief').

Step 14 — MISSION TASK TOAST: In MissionControlScreen.tsx, add a useEffect that watches completedTaskIds from useMissionProgressStore. When a new taskId appears, show a toast '⭐ Task complete: {taskLabel}!' for 3 seconds. Keep a ref of previously seen taskIds to detect newly completed ones.

Step 15 — BASECONFIG DURATION SELECTOR: In src/features/base-configuration/BaseConfigurationScreen.tsx, add a mission duration section after the existing configuration fields. Render 3 buttons: '30 days', '60 days', '90 days'. Selected button has teal background (PrimaryButton variant='primary'). Unselected use variant='secondary'. On click, call missionStore.getState().setMissionDuration(days). Preview text below: '30 days: Quick mission — great for beginners. 60 days: Standard challenge. 90 days: Expert — survive the full mission!' Read selectedMissionDurationDays from useMissionStore to show current selection.

MissionControlScreen shows failure overlay on failure outcome with fault state list
